findings.text: §3 still proposes a "resumable execution ledger" as a thing to build, while reckon/ledger.py owns the durable run-with-commits record and reckon/crew/run_store.py owns the shadow store the plan's own followups already report landing against

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §5 and the landed §2–§4 records add guards and call sites inside the existing deep module reckon/crew/promotion.py; no new module is proposed whose interface would be narrower than what it hides.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the open outcome distinctions already have owners in reckon/crew/promotion.py and reckon/crew/recovery.py, and §3's "resumable execution ledger" names machinery reckon/ledger.py already owns.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §5 hides several distinct open repairs behind one plan-vocabulary sentence and cites no file, function or repair list, so a worker cannot tell what already exists from what to build.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no proposal in the plan adds a thin forwarding layer over existing machinery; §5 strengthens refusals inside an existing module rather than wrapping it.
